quote: But he that dares not grasp the thorn / Should never crave the rose.
source: Anne Brontë, The Narrow Way (1848), lines 15 to 16, in The Complete Poems of Anne Brontë (ed. Clement Shorter, 1920)

evidence.where: Wikisource transcription of The Complete Poems of Anne Brontë, ed. Clement Shorter (1920), the poem read in full
evidence.edition: The Complete Poems of Anne Brontë, ed. Clement Shorter (London: Hodder and Stoughton, 1920); first printed in Fraser’s Magazine, December 1848, as by Acton Bell
evidence.locator: The Narrow Way, fourth stanza, lines 15 to 16; the poem is signed A. B. and dated April 27, 1848

reason: The couplet closes the fourth stanza of The Narrow Way in exactly this wording and lineation in the Shorter edition, whose header gives the Fraser’s Magazine printing of December 1848. It is the poem’s best known sentence. Not shipped, Anne Brontë unused (Charlotte is a different person), not banned.
